clue.text: Wanted 100K pumped into revolutionary business arrangement

indicators.note: something pumped into a container ends up inside it, so these letters go into the middle
a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a deal is an arrangement struck in business
C is the Roman numeral for 100, and K stands as itself

explanation.surface: Someone was short of a hundred thousand, invested in a radical business scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses the arrangement word; 'pumped into' puts C (Roman 100) and K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacked and wanted are synonyms in the sense of being without or short of something.

clue.text: Boosts standings during competition

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a cup is a competition such as the FA Cup
standings in a league table are its ranks

explanation.surface: Positions in a league table get a lift while a tournament is being played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places the standings within the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To crank up is a phrasal verb for increasing or intensifying, so it fits the verb boosts.

clue.text: Attention Deficit Disorder leads to naughty child wearing skimpy outfit

indicators.note: someone wearing an outfit is inside it, so the outfit's letters go around the others

parts.note: a negligee is a flimsy, revealing nightdress

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A medical condition is blamed for a badly behaved child in a revealing costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes N and C from 'naughty child'; 'wearing' puts them inside NEGLIGEE, between its last two E's.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligence is a failure to take proper care, a lack of attention, read here playfully as a medical-sounding condition.

clue.text: Run over Maxim without a trace of remorse for this reason

definitions.text: Run over Maxim without a trace of remorse for this reason

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: in older usage without means outside, so these letters go around the next piece

parts.note: an adage is a maxim or saying

indicators.note: just a trace of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone flattened Maxim without any regret, and here is why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: ADAGE goes around R, the first letter taken by 'a trace of', giving ADRAGE after R and O. Read as a whole, the clue describes an angry driver who knocks someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury at the wheel is the motive behind a driver deliberately knocking someone down without remorse.

clue.text: Resist attitude on which work depends

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a pose is an attitude struck by the body

explanation.surface: A refusal to give in is described as a stance that a job relies on.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the work sits above the attitude, so the pose holds the work up: this is the sense of 'on which work depends'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppose and resist are synonymous verbs for standing against something.

clue.text: See 23
Plant pests almost overwhelming bottom half of garden

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is three of its letters, here the opening three
almost means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: lice are parasitic insect pests

explanation.surface: Insect pests have nearly taken over the lower part of a garden's plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter of the pests; 'overwhelming bottom' places the shortened pests at the foot of this down answer, beneath the top half of 'garden'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic is a bulbous plant of the onion family grown for its pungent cloves.

clue.text: Tyrannical cops tied up

indicators.note: a thing that is tied up or mixed up has had its parts jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police officers bound hand and foot, as a tyrant might leave them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tied' looks like part of the definition's scene, but it is fodder alongside 'cops'; 'up' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a tyrant, so the adjective formed from it means tyrannical.

clue.text: Where one might see air aflutter with eagle's wings

definitions.text: Where one might see air aflutter with eagle's wings

indicators.note: letters set aflutter are flapped about into a new order

parts.note: the wings of the word eagle are its outer letters, E and E

explanation.surface: A description of a lofty nest, with the air stirred by the beating of an eagle's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: AIR plus the two E's from the ends of 'eagle' are shuffled; the whole clue also describes the nest itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerie (or eyrie) is the high nest of a bird of prey, the place an eagle beats its wings.

clue.text: Place to raise issue that no one cares for

definitions.text: Place to raise issue that no one cares for

parts.words: Place to raise issue that no one cares for
parts.note: issue means offspring, and children with no parents to care for them were raised in such an institution; the surface suggests an ignored complaint

explanation.surface: A forum for bringing up a complaint nobody is interested in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise issue' looks like bringing up a topic, and 'no one cares for' like indifference; really issue is children, raised there because no parent looks after them.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution housing children without parents is a place where offspring nobody looks after are brought up.

clue.text: Lend novel to transfix child that's read e-book apparently

indicators.note: something transfixed is pierced right through, so these letters go into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of lend are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A lending library hands out a novel to grip a youngster who uses an e-reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges the first word and 'to transfix' sets it inside the child. The definition jokes on Kindle, the e-reader, as though it were a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a made-up verb from Amazon's Kindle reader, a book read that way has been 'Kindled'; the real word means set alight.

clue.text: Drink too much to do more than meet?

parts.note: over means excessively, as in overdo
to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether drinking to excess goes beyond simply meeting up.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in the opposite order: the drink comes last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that overlap go beyond touching at an edge and actually share part of their extent.

clue.text: Appointed court accepting electronic evidence

indicators.note: a thing accepting another takes it in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: to court someone is to date them
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a sign is evidence or an indication of something

explanation.surface: A law court has been named and agrees to admit digital proof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' is a verb (to woo), not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Designate as an adjective after a noun, as in chair designate, means appointed but not yet in office.

clue.text: One assuming discretion is taken for granted

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the discretion takes these letters inside

parts.note: tact is discretion in dealing with people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who presumes they are being discreet is treated as a given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One assuming' reads as a person presuming, but 'assuming' means taking on: TACT takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood or implied without being stated, which is to say taken for granted.

clue.text: Go too far with Spooner's old woman's hairpiece?

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words that follow

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, an old woman, and the 's is kept
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A wig belonging to a grandmother is so outrageous it oversteps the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAN'S TRESS with the initial sounds GR and TR swapped gives TRANS GRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress is to step beyond a limit or rule, which is going too far.

clue.text: Enlarged photo padded with most up-to-date packaging material

parts.note: expanded means enlarged

indicators.note: something padded with a filling has it inside, so these letters go into the middle

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
the last news is the latest, most up-to-date

explanation.surface: A blown-up photograph has been cushioned with the newest wrapping stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most up-to-date' gives LAST, as in the last word on a subject; 'padded with' sets it inside the photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Expanded polystyrene and similar foamed plastics are widely used to protect goods in transit.

clue.text: One's prepared for drinking sprees getting messy like this

indicators.note: letters getting messy are thrown into disorder, so these are rearranged

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A drink made ready for people on binges that turn chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting messy' scrambles 'sprees'; 'One's prepared for drinking' is the definition, not a person getting ready to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong black coffee is a thing made to be drunk, an example of a prepared beverage.

clue.text: Chapter 1 reviewed method of proportional representation

indicators.note: reviewed suggests revised and reorganised, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The opening section of a book looks again at a fair electoral voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proportional representation' looks electoral, but here it means a diagram showing proportions as slices.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular diagram divided into slices shows each part's share of the whole, a visual representation of proportions.

clue.text: Engines generated energy in short bursts

indicators.note: generated means produced or made up, so these letters are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: short means missing its final letter

explanation.surface: Machines produced power in brief spurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the final S from 'bursts', leaving BURST; with E and IN that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbines are rotary machines driven by steam, gas or water, a kind of engine.

clue.text: See 20
Leaves carpeting spaceship

definitions.meaning: salad leaves of the plant also called arugula
a carpeting is a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: Foliage covers the floor of a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'carpeting' is British slang for a stern reprimand, and so is a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a peppery salad plant, a severe reprimand and a vehicle launched into space.

clue.text: Perhaps one keeping notes is tense about a certain record's source

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
re means about or concerning
sure means certain

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone who jots things down is nervous about where a particular record came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' are banknotes, money held for a club, not jottings.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who looks after a society's funds keeps its banknotes, so is an example of someone keeping notes.

clue.text: A motto associated with this fruit concentrate

definitions.note: the clue words are linked with the paste because the paste's name, read as wordplay, produces them; the paste itself is a fruit concentrate

parts.note: mash, so the answer read as an instruction mashes the fruit's name, and those six letters rearranged spell these two clue words

explanation.surface: A slogan is linked with a particular fruit paste.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the second word of the answer acts as an anagram signal on the first, and that mash-up produces 'A motto'. The solver reads 'this fruit concentrate' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick sieved paste made from cooked red fruit is sold in tubes as a concentrate for sauces.

clue.text: Portion of tagliatelle served up to make use of eBay?

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
a portion of the words is a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Some pasta has been plated up, to be sold online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portion of' finds LLESER in 'tagliatelle served'; 'up' turns it round in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: eBay is a website for selling goods second-hand, so using it means selling on something already bought.

clue.text: Come out with contents of next demand

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters

parts.note: a claim is a demand for something owed

explanation.surface: Revealing what is inside the following request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of' takes EX from inside 'next'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out or blurt out words, which is coming out with them.

clue.text: Sort out a team to exploit manufacturing technology

indicators.note: to sort letters is to put them in a new order

explanation.surface: A manager reorganises a squad so they can take advantage of factory methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort out' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'out' is fodder with 'a team'.
explanation.definitionFit: To automate is to introduce machines to do work previously done by hand, using manufacturing technology.

clue.text: Bombast that woman regularly picked to pieces

parts.note: her refers to that woman

indicators.note: letters regularly picked are taken at even intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: A particular woman's overblown talk has been torn apart by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly picked' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'to pieces': O, I, C, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroics can mean extravagant, high-flown language, the same as bombast.

clue.text: Observer magazine's leading article is pulled

indicators.note: an article that is pulled is withdrawn, so these letters are removed

parts.note: A British weekly political magazine
the definite article, at the front of the magazine's title

explanation.surface: A newspaper magazine has its editorial withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the Sunday newspaper but is the definition. 'leading article' looks like an editorial; it is THE, at the front of the title The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is someone who watches an event, an observer.

clue.text: What may be seen as least appropriate?

indicators.note: letters seen as something else are being read in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about which choice is the least suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for oneself without permission, which is a synonym for theft.
